image_description: An underwater close-up shot of a grey whale's head and upper torso. The image highlights the characteristic mottled grey skin covered in white barnacle patches (callosities). The rostrum is visible, along with one pectoral flipper tucked against the body. The lighting is dim, typical of underwater photography, with particulate matter in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle of the photo shows the side/underside of the head; the top of the rostrum and blowholes are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture clearly displays the chaotic mottling and distinct white clusters characteristic of cyamids and barnacles found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image frame cuts off before reaching the dorsal region of the whale's back.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior section is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified from this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint; the visible body skin matches the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or obscured by shadow/angle; internal baleen structures are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, paddle-shaped flipper is clearly visible in the lower-left quadrant, appearing anatomically correct for a cetacean.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: High-frequency detail in the skin texture confirms the rough, bumpy surface associated with callosities.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight smudging or 'painterly' blur in the water background near the top left, lacking the natural particulate randomness of real underwater photography, though subtle.
Edges of the flipper blend slightly into the dark water without sharp occlusion boundaries, common in AI generation but also possible in low-light photography.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification that the subject is indeed a grey whale and not another baleen species (e.g., humpback) based on skin pattern.
To check for seamless integration of the flipper with the body and ensure no floating artifacts or boundary bleeding in the dark water.
To assess if the noise/grain looks like natural ISO noise or AI-generated texture smoothing/artifacts.

focus_areas: Flipper anatomy and connection to body
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'mottled' skin pattern. AI often struggles with consistent high-frequency noise like barnacles, sometimes repeating patterns or smearing them. Verify if the barnacles look physically attached or just painted on. Also, check the flipper's leading edge for structural plausibility.
